title: What Everyone Gets Wrong About Gambling on Sports
summary: First-hand account of arbitrage sports betting across sportsbooks and promos: profitable but quickly limited, with a warning that ordinary bettors lose.

assertions.quote: There’s no such thing as a pro craps player because you can’t get a positive EV in craps.

verdicts.note: House edge on these games is fixed by the rules; only card counting and skill games have known positive-EV play.

assertions.quote: Good sports betting is not a measure of sports knowledge. It is a measure of pricing knowledge.

verdicts.note: Arbitrage and closing-line-value approaches are the documented edges, but they are small and short-lived.

assertions.quote: if you know how to place both sides of an outcome, you can reliably turn those bonus bets into real withdrawable cash

verdicts.note: Matched betting on promos is a well-documented small, one-time profit source.

assertions.quote: You can have one bet voided for any reason, and suddenly your arb that nets 50 bucks could turn into a $500 loss.

verdicts.note: Voided legs and palpable-error rules are standard sportsbook terms and are a known arb risk.

assertions.quote: You will get banned very quickly from any sportsbook for advantaged gambling.

verdicts.note: Limiting of winning accounts is widely reported and acknowledged by the books themselves.
A footnote states that sports betting sites often cut off or limit bets from bettors who win too often, citing a WSJ report rather than the paper's own data.

assertions.quote: This idea that most of the guys betting on sports every weekend are “pretty much breaking even” is wrong.
sportsbooks want to serve you “smart info” from smart guys with detailed spreadsheets and verifiable data because it ignores pricing

verdicts.note: A plausible incentive, but the motive is inferred rather than demonstrated.

assertions.quote: a 50/50 coin flip isn’t sold at +100 odds, not even -105 or -110, but -115

verdicts.note: Standard vig is around 4-5% on -110 lines; some markets are juiced higher, but the extreme figure is not typical.

assertions.quote: You can pay like 75 bucks a month for access to automated software that tells you what you bet on

verdicts.note: Such tools exist and work until accounts are limited, which happens fast.

assertions.quote: falling into a gambling addiction is a strong indicator for financial ruin and early death

verdicts.note: Problem gambling is associated with bankruptcy, debt, and suicide in the public health literature.

Betting access causes more overdrafts, more credit card debt and overextended borrowers among constrained households, and the authors argue these effects will not self-correct because betting is addictive; addiction is not measured directly and outcomes fall short of ruin.
